coverage.scope: Telegram Bot API error responses, reviewed against source with selected hosted observations. Live verification is incomplete; see each record’s evidence.
coverage.examples: Synthetic examples derived from the cited source.

entries.summary: The requested message content and reply markup are unchanged.

match_any.description_exact: Bad Request: message is not modified: specified new message content and reply markup are exactly the same as a current content and reply markup of the message

possible_causes: The requested edit repeats the current content and markup.
entries.diagnostic_limits: The response does not include the current message or establish the history of concurrent edits.

evidence.note: Editing a newly created bot message with identical text returned this description. The test message was then deleted.
MESSAGE_NOT_MODIFIED is rewritten here; prefix and initial-case handling are at lines 165-205.

response.description: Bad Request: message is not modified: specified new message content and reply markup are exactly the same as a current content and reply markup of the message

preconditions: The application considers an already-applied desired state a successful outcome.

entries.summary: Telegram rejected deletion of the message.

match_any.description_exact: Bad Request: message can't be deleted

possible_causes: A permissions, message-type or message-age restriction may prevent deletion.
entries.diagnostic_limits: The source proves the response mapping, not which deletion restriction caused a particular failure. The causes above are diagnostic hypotheses.

evidence.note: MESSAGE_DELETE_FORBIDDEN is rewritten before the Bad Request prefix is added.

response.description: Bad Request: message can't be deleted

preconditions: Check the current deleteMessage rules and bot permissions; a permanent message restriction may have no repair.

entries.summary: The query ID is invalid or its response window has expired.

match_any.description_exact: Bad Request: query is too old and response timeout expired or query ID is invalid

possible_causes: The query identifier is invalid.
The response arrived after the query's response window.
entries.diagnostic_limits: The description explicitly combines causes; it does not establish a universal timeout duration.

evidence.note: QUERY_ID_INVALID is deliberately expanded to a description containing alternatives.

response.description: Bad Request: query is too old and response timeout expired or query ID is invalid

preconditions: Use the identifier from the correct incoming query and respond promptly to future queries.

entries.summary: The bot could not resolve this chat.

match_any.description_exact: Bad Request: chat not found

possible_causes: An upstream lookup error was replaced with the generic chat lookup message.
A username resolved to a chat type that this lookup does not allow.
entries.diagnostic_limits: This is not proof that the chat was deleted, the bot was blocked, or the identifier is permanently unusable.

evidence.note: A fallback masks upstream 400-class errors, and a separate local branch emits the same description.
Some upstream codes are converted to 400 before the fallback description is applied.

response.description: Bad Request: chat not found

preconditions: Verify the identifier, target type and bot access before changing stored chat records.

entries.summary: The group has moved to a supergroup with a new ID.
possible_causes: The request addresses a group that was upgraded to a supergroup.
entries.diagnostic_limits: Use the structured replacement identifier; a description alone does not supply the new target.

evidence.note: getChatAdministrators on an already migrated basic group returned the migration parameter. Its value is synthetic in the report.
The replacement chat ID is placed in response parameters.
Documents migrate_to_chat_id, including its maximum of 52 significant bits.

response.description: Bad Request: group chat was upgraded to a supergroup chat

preconditions: Update the intended chat reference from parameters.migrate_to_chat_id, account for concurrent updates, and bound retries.

entries.summary: The user has blocked the bot.

match_any.description_exact: Forbidden: bot was blocked by the user

possible_causes: The recipient has blocked the bot.
entries.diagnostic_limits: The response establishes the current rejection, not that access can never be restored.

evidence.note: USER_IS_BLOCKED changes both the code (to 403) and the description.

response.description: Forbidden: bot was blocked by the user

preconditions: Use application policy to track reachability and resume only when there is evidence that access changed.

entries.summary: The server asks the bot to wait before trying again.
possible_causes: Flood limiting.
Authorization or startup throttling.
An unfinished query being disposed, including during shutdown.
entries.diagnostic_limits: The response does not identify whether the limit is per chat, per bot, per method or caused by server lifecycle handling.

evidence.note: Builds both the description and structured retry_after parameter.
The query deleter also produces this response with a five-second delay.
Flood and authorization paths share the response shape.
Documents retry_after in seconds.

response.description: Too Many Requests: retry after 5

preconditions: Wait at least the supplied delay, coordinate with any framework retry plugin, and bound attempts.

entries.summary: Polling was requested while a webhook is active or being configured.

match_any.description_exact: Conflict: can't use getUpdates method while webhook is active; use deleteWebhook to delete the webhook first

possible_causes: The bot has an active or pending webhook configuration.
entries.diagnostic_limits: This is a different condition from two simultaneous getUpdates requests.

evidence.note: Checks configured and pending webhook state before polling.

response.description: Conflict: can't use getUpdates method while webhook is active; use deleteWebhook to delete the webhook first

preconditions: If polling is intended, remove the webhook deliberately; if webhooks are intended, stop polling.

entries.summary: Another getUpdates request interrupted the pending long poll.

match_any.description_exact: Conflict: terminated by other getUpdates request; make sure that only one bot instance is running

possible_causes: Overlapping getUpdates requests for the same bot.
entries.diagnostic_limits: Overlapping requests may originate in one process or multiple deployments; the response does not prove how many bot processes exist.

evidence.note: The alternate branch emits a different description for termination by setWebhook.

response.description: Conflict: terminated by other getUpdates request; make sure that only one bot instance is running

preconditions: Stop competing polling loops or establish ownership before resuming.

entries.summary: The server rejected the token during local validation.

match_any.description_exact: Unauthorized: invalid token specified

possible_causes: A locally checked token structure or numeric identifier constraint failed.
entries.diagnostic_limits: This signature is narrower than generic Unauthorized. Other malformed-token paths may produce different codes.

evidence.note: Two local checks return this exact response; the intervening check can return 421.

response.description: Unauthorized: invalid token specified

preconditions: Verify the configured token without placing it in logs or inventory submissions.

entries.summary: The file exceeds the server’s non-local download limit.

match_any.description_exact: Bad Request: file is too big

scope.deployment: Source guard applies when local_mode is false.

possible_causes: Expected or downloaded file size exceeds MAX_DOWNLOAD_FILE_SIZE while local mode is disabled.
entries.diagnostic_limits: A bare file-is-too-big description without method context is insufficient for this download-specific classification. This is not an upload-size rule.

evidence.note: getFile reaches the size check guarded by local_mode.
The download update path enforces the same limit.
The constant is 20 << 20 bytes in this revision.

response.description: Bad Request: file is too big

preconditions: Use a suitable smaller file or deliberately configure a server with the required local-mode download capability.

entries.summary: The bot client is closing for a server restart.

match_any.description_exact: Internal Server Error: restart

possible_causes: The bot client is closing without taking the logout branches.
entries.diagnostic_limits: An exception wrapper that discarded the original 5xx description cannot recover this distinction from the status alone.

evidence.note: The closing error is passed directly to fail_query by fail_query_closing.

response.description: Internal Server Error: restart

preconditions: Apply bounded backoff and evaluate whether repeating the particular operation is safe; do not derive replay safety from a 5xx status alone.

entries.summary: The token failed the server’s bot-ID or routing check.

match_any.description_exact: Misdirected Request: forbidden token specified

scope.deployment: Relevant to the open-source server's token-range routing; hosted occurrence is unverified.

possible_causes: The bot ID is outside the server’s configured token range.
The token’s numeric prefix could not be parsed.
entries.diagnostic_limits: The same response covers a routing failure and a token-format failure; it does not prove that Telegram revoked the token.

evidence.note: Both sides of the condition emit the same 421 response.

response.description: Misdirected Request: forbidden token specified

preconditions: Check token formatting and, when operating a local server, its token-range configuration.

entries.summary: The bot session has logged out.

match_any.description_exact: Logged out

possible_causes: The server is completing a bot logout.
entries.diagnostic_limits: Not every 400 response begins with Bad Request. This signature alone does not explain why logout was initiated.

evidence.note: Stores a 400 description with no Bad Request prefix.
The direct fail_query path preserves that description.

response.description: Logged out

preconditions: Determine whether logout or a server move was intentional before resuming requests.

entries.summary: The uploaded webhook certificate exceeds the server’s size limit.

match_any.description_template: Bad Request: certificate size is too big ({size_bytes} bytes)

possible_causes: The uploaded certificate file is larger than MAX_CERTIFICATE_FILE_SIZE.
entries.diagnostic_limits: The captured size describes the rejected upload; it is not the configured limit or a Telegram media limit.

evidence.note: The description interpolates the actual file size; one literal string cannot represent all responses.
The constant is 3 << 20 bytes in this revision.

response.description: Bad Request: certificate size is too big (4194304 bytes)

preconditions: Verify that the uploaded file is the intended certificate and satisfies this server revision's limit.
